name: bootstrap-visualizer-extension
description: Visual editor for Bootstrap grid layouts in Angular templates.

bootstrapVisualizer.defaultBreakpoint.markdownDescription: Breakpoint the canvas opens at. Switching breakpoints in the canvas is temporary and does not change this.

bootstrapVisualizer.stretchToFit.markdownDescription: Open with the sheet stretched to the full canvas panel instead of the breakpoint's representative width. The **Stretch to fit** checkbox in the canvas updates this.

bootstrapVisualizer.tintOverfullRows.markdownDescription: Open with overfull rows tinted amber. The **Tint overfull rows** checkbox in the canvas updates this.

enumDescriptions: New columns use col-*/col-md-* and offset-* (Bootstrap 4/5)
New columns use col-xs-*/col-sm-* and col-sm-offset-* (Bootstrap 3)
bootstrapVisualizer.dialect.markdownDescription: Class style for **new** columns when a file has no grid classes to detect from. A file that already uses one dialect always keeps it.

bootstrapVisualizer.newRowClasses.markdownDescription: Extra classes on every row the canvas **creates**, added after `row` — e.g. `clearfix form-group` writes `<div class="row clearfix form-group">`. A project convention, so it can be committed in the workspace's `.vscode/settings.json`. Grid classes (`col-*`, `offset-*`) and `row` itself are ignored here — the canvas writes those.

bootstrapVisualizer.newColumnClasses.markdownDescription: Extra classes on every column the canvas **creates**, added after the computed `col-*` classes — e.g. `px-2` writes `<div class="col-md-6 px-2">`. A project convention, so it can be committed in the workspace's `.vscode/settings.json`. Grid classes are ignored here; widths and offsets come from the inspector's steppers.

bootstrapVisualizer.liveSync.markdownDescription: Keep the canvas in sync with the editor **as you type** (after a short pause). On by default: canvas edits go straight to the buffer, so following the editor can never lose your work, and the editor's own undo no longer parks the canvas. Turn it off to have the canvas hold still while you type and wait for a save or **Resync** instead. Either way, canvas edits are verified against the file before they touch it, so a half-typed buffer can't corrupt it.

scripts.build: npm run build:webview && npm run build:host
scripts.test:vscode: npm run build && npm run build:tests && vscode-test
scripts.vsix: npm run build && npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --out releases/
